output.summary: An evergreen, tree-like palm native to the far southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico. Its waxy fan-shaped leaves have long white threads between their segments, and its sweet fruit pulp is eaten raw, cooked or ground into flour; the bud is also eaten.
output.edibilityNote: Sweet fruit pulp was eaten raw, cooked or as flour by Native Americans; the bud, or heart of palm, is also eaten.
